dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real-valued function X on a measure space, this predicate says that X is measurable and that there exists a real K > 0 for which LocalDef004 holds.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

binders: There exists one real constant C, chosen before and independently of every probability space, index type, measure, and random-variable family.

After C is chosen: for every type iota in an arbitrary universe equipped with a Fintype instance, including the empty finite type; for every type Omega in an arbitrary universe equipped with a measurable-space structure; for every measure mu on Omega equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance; and for every family X : iota -> Omega -> Real.
hypotheses: For every i in iota, X_i is sub-Gaussian in the componentwise LocalDef001 sense: it is Borel measurable and has some real scale K_i > 0 for which exp(X_i^2 / K_i^2) is integrable and has mu-integral at most 2.
For every i in iota, X_i is integrable with respect to mu and is centered exactly: integral X_i dmu = 0.
The full indexed family (X_i) is mutually independent with respect to mu, in the iIndepFun sense.
conclusions: The pointwise unweighted finite sum S(omega) = sum over all i in iota of X_i(omega) is itself sub-Gaussian in the same LocalDef001 sense.

The squared real value of the intrinsic PsiTwoNorm of S is at most C times the unweighted sum of the squared real values of the intrinsic PsiTwoNorms of the components: (LocalDef002(mu,S).toReal)^2 <= C * sum_i (LocalDef002(mu,X_i).toReal)^2.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001(mu,Y) means: Y is measurable and there exists a real K > 0 such that Y is measurable, exp(Y^2/K^2) is integrable, and its mu-integral is at most 2.
For an ENNReal t, LocalDef006(mu,Y,t) means: Y is measurable; t != 0 and t != infinity; exp(Y^2/(t.toReal)^2) is integrable; and its mu-integral is at most 2.

The intrinsic PsiTwoNorm LocalDef002(mu,Y) is the ENNReal infimum of all t satisfying LocalDef006(mu,Y,t). The theorem's inequality applies ENNReal.toReal to this infimum and then squares the resulting real number.
All sums are Finset.univ sums over the entire finite index type and hence are unweighted; for an empty index type they are empty sums equal to zero.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a single absolute real constant C >= 1 such that, uniformly for every arbitrary finite index type iota (including the empty type), every probability measure mu on any measurable sample space Omega, and every real-valued family (X_i) on that space, if each X_i is componentwise sub-Gaussian, integrable, and centered and the family is mutually independent, then the pointwise unweighted sum S = sum_i X_i is again sub-Gaussian and its squared intrinsic PsiTwoNorm, after the definition's explicit ENNReal.toReal conversion, satisfies ||S||_Psi2^2 <= C sum_i ||X_i||_Psi2^2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The existential quantifier for C precedes all family and probability-space binders, so C cannot depend on iota, Omega, mu, or X.

The index type is only required to be finite; it is not required to be nonempty. For empty iota the family hypotheses are vacuous, S is the zero function, and the asserted closure and inequality specialize to the zero-function case with an empty right-hand sum.
The statement concerns real-valued functions on one common probability space and only the unweighted sum with every coefficient equal to one.

Sub-Gaussianity is componentwise and explicitly includes measurability plus existence of a positive real exponential-square scale. Integrability and exact zero integral of each X_i are separately assumed.
Independence is mutual indexed-family independence via iIndepFun, not merely pairwise independence.

The intrinsic quantity is defined in ENNReal as an infimum over finite nonzero ENNReal scales, but the displayed inequality compares squares only after ENNReal.toReal. The statement does not separately insert explicit finiteness or nonzero hypotheses for the infima at the inequality site.
The conclusion includes both sub-Gaussian closure of the sum and the quantitative squared inequality; neither conjunct may be dropped.
No positivity, atomlessness, nondegeneracy, cardinality lower bound, identical-distribution assumption, or scalar weights are imposed beyond the displayed hypotheses.
The theorem asserts existence of some C >= 1; it does not assert an exact or optimal value of C.
